newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Caldera says bonus to raise minimum wage.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Caldera says bonus to raise minimum wage.

text.p: Venezuelan President Rafael Caldera said Friday the government was studying an increase in the minimum wage with a temporary bonus.
Asked if the bonus would be granted on May 1 if Congress had not yet finished discussions of pending Labor Law reforms, he told reporters: "We are studying this, we are very optimistic."
Some government officials fear that raising the minimum wage with a so-called "bridging bonus" before the reforms are approved will kill all incentive legislators may have for acting swiftly.

No decision has been made on the size of the wage increase but government officials and political sources said the raise would take the minimum wage to between 68,000 and 75,000 bolivars ($142-156) per month from the current 53,000, including bonuses.
The reforms before Congress form part of wide-ranging changes aimed at opening up Venezuela's labor markets and revamping its crumbling social security system.
